decks.name: LeetCode #417 - Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
decks.description: Find all cells where water can flow to both Pacific and Atlantic oceans given height map

cards.question: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow: There is an m x n rectangular island that borders both the Pacific Ocean and Atlantic Ocean. The Pacific Ocean touches the island's left and top edges, and the Atlantic Ocean touches the island's right and bottom edges. The island is partitioned into a grid of square cells. You are given an m x n integer matrix heights where heights[r][c] represents the height above sea level of the cell at coordinate (r, c). Water can only flow in four directions (up, down, left, or right) from a cell to another one with height equal or lower. Find all cells where water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans. Return a list of grid coordinates.

solutions.name: Brute Force (Backtracking)
solutions.explanation: For each cell, use DFS with backtracking to explore all downhill paths to check if it reaches both oceans. Use nonlocal flags for pacific and atlantic. DFS explores all four directions, checking if water can flow (current height >= neighbor height). Mark cell as visited by setting to infinity during exploration, restore after. If DFS goes out of bounds on top/left, set pacific flag. If out of bounds on bottom/right, set atlantic flag. For each cell, reset flags and run DFS. If both flags set, add cell to result. Very inefficient as it explores all possible paths from every cell. Time O(m*n*4^(m*n)) in worst case. Space O(m*n) for recursion stack.

solutions.timeDescription: For each of m*n cells, we explore all possible downhill paths. In worst case with all equal heights, each path can branch into 4 directions at each step, leading to exponential time complexity
solutions.spaceDescription: Recursion stack can go up to m*n depth in worst case when exploring entire grid from a single cell
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given heights [[1,2,2,3,5],[3,2,3,4,4],[2,4,5,3,1],[6,7,1,4,5],[5,1,1,2,4]]: For cell (0,4) with height 5, DFS explores downhill: can reach top edge (Pacific) by going up, can reach right edge (Atlantic) by going right. Both flags set, add to result. For cell (1,3) with height 4, DFS explores: reaches top (Pacific) and bottom (Atlantic), add to result. Repeat for all cells. Very slow due to exhaustive path exploration.

solutions.name: Depth First Search
solutions.explanation: Start from ocean borders and work backwards to find all reachable cells. Create two sets for cells reachable from Pacific and Atlantic. Run DFS from all Pacific border cells (top row and left column) flowing uphill (to higher or equal cells). Run DFS from all Atlantic border cells (bottom row and right column) flowing uphill. DFS adds cells to visited set and recursively explores neighbors with height >= current. Return cells in intersection of both sets. Much more efficient as each cell visited at most twice (once per ocean). Time O(m*n) visiting each cell constant times. Space O(m*n) for two sets.

solutions.timeDescription: Each cell is visited at most twice: once during Pacific DFS and once during Atlantic DFS. Both DFS traversals together visit all cells in linear time
solutions.spaceDescription: Two sets store up to m*n coordinates each. Recursion stack can go up to m*n depth in worst case
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given heights [[1,2,2,3,5],[3,2,3,4,4],[2,4,5,3,1],[6,7,1,4,5],[5,1,1,2,4]]: Start DFS from Pacific borders (top row and left column). From (0,0) height 1, explore uphill to reachable cells. From (0,1) height 2, explore uphill. Continue for all border cells, building Pacific set. Start DFS from Atlantic borders (bottom row and right column). From (4,4) height 4, explore uphill. Continue building Atlantic set. Find intersection: cells like (0,4), (1,3), (1,4), (2,2), (3,0), (3,1), (4,0) are in both sets. Return these coordinates.

solutions.name: Breadth First Search
solutions.explanation: Same approach as DFS but using BFS from ocean borders. Create two boolean matrices for Pacific and Atlantic reachability. Build list of Pacific border cells (top row and left column) and Atlantic border cells (bottom row and right column). Run BFS from Pacific sources, marking reachable cells in Pacific matrix. Flow is uphill (to cells with height >= current). Run BFS from Atlantic sources, marking reachable cells in Atlantic matrix. Return cells where both matrices are true. BFS processes cells level by level rather than depth-first. Time O(m*n) as each cell processed once per ocean. Space O(m*n) for matrices and queue.
